rules: Searched every PubMed record in Europe PMC with vitamin E (vitamin E, alpha-tocopherol, tocopherol, tocopheryl) in its title or abstract; downloaded all reviews, randomised trials and guidelines.
Left out animal studies (MeSH tags, or the title when there are none) and retracted papers.
An outcome counts when its words are in the title.

Reviews: meta-analyses or systematic reviews of randomised trials of giving vitamin E, with vitamin E in the title, or in the abstract of a review of several supplements (not reviews of blood levels in observational studies; reviews without an abstract are kept for screening), and not about another group of people (such as sepsis, intensive care or surgery; each outcome's list is in the search definition). Chosen: the three newest meta-analyses (systematic reviews only if fewer than three), plus the most comprehensive one (most trials pooled, read from the abstract). Citations are shown but do not choose.
Newer large trials: randomised trials of at least 1,000 people (read from the abstract) from the year of the newest chosen review on, which those reviews may not include.

Screening: each eligible review's title and abstract was read against the finding's question (who, what was given, compared with what, what was measured) by Claude Code (opus), titles and abstracts only. Only reviews that answer it can be chosen; the others are listed with the reason. The decisions are kept in the repository and have not yet been checked by a clinician.
Overlap: the chosen reviews' reference lists (from Europe PMC) matched against the downloaded vitamin E trials, measured as the corrected covered area (Pieper 2014, PMID 24581293).

left.title: Vitamin E and heart disease: a thematic systematic review
left.reason: Asks about vitamin E and heart disease outcomes, but it is a thematic review of 58 papers with no pooled analysis of randomised trials reported.

left.title: From A to E: Uniting vitamins against stroke risk-A systematic review and network meta-analysis
left.reason: Compares vitamins including vitamin E vs placebo for stroke, but pools cohort studies together with randomised trials.

left.title: The effects of magnesium and vitamin E co-supplementation on some cardiovascular risk factors: A meta-analysis
left.reason: Vitamin E is only given with magnesium in people with metabolic disorders, and the outcomes are blood markers, not heart attacks or strokes.

left.title: Meta-analysis of the association of the haptoglobin genotype with cardiovascular outcomes and the pharmacogenomic interactions with vitamin E supplementation
left.reason: Vitamin E and cardiovascular events match, but the vitamin E analysis covers only diabetic patients with the Hp 2-2 genotype, a narrower group.

left.title: Dietary supplements and risk of cause-specific death, cardiovascular disease, and cancer: a protocol for a systematic review and network meta-analysis of primary prevention trials
left.reason: Vitamin E and heart outcomes are planned in primary prevention trials, but this is a protocol with no pooled results and includes adults from age 18.

left.title: Effect of antioxidant vitamin supplementation on cardiovascular outcomes: a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
left.reason: Pools antioxidant vitamins (E, beta-carotene, C) together vs placebo; the abstract gives no separate vitamin E result.

left.title: Haptoglobin genotype and cardiovascular outcomes in diabetes mellitus - natural history of the disease and the effect of vitamin E treatment. Meta-analysis of the medical literature
left.reason: Vitamin E trials in diabetes with cardiovascular outcomes, but the analysis is split by haptoglobin genotype, a narrower group.

left.title: Interactions of commonly used dietary supplements with cardiovascular drugs: a systematic review
left.reason: Vitamin E is added to aspirin versus aspirin alone, with one trial reporting a cardiovascular composite; the review studies supplement-drug interactions, not pooled prevention.

left.title: Vitamin E supplementation in cardiovascular disease and cancer prevention: Part 1
left.reason: Reviews vitamin E trials for cardiovascular prevention, but it is a narrative review with no pooled analysis.

left.title: Antioxidant vitamins in the prevention of cardiovascular disease: a systematic review
left.reason: Reviews antioxidant vitamin trials for heart attack and stroke, but the abstract gives no separate vitamin E results and no clear pooling.
